rationale: The aim is to improve weaning on one ward within one season while adapting the protocol, especially its night-time delivery. Improvement cycles with weekly run charts suit this: the change is supported for infants aged 8 weeks or older (c1, c2), night delivery needs adapting between cycles (c4), and safety is watched with balancing measures. A before-after cohort comparison of two winters was considered and refused because season severity and staffing differ between years and a fixed protocol could not be adapted. The conflicting evidence on younger infants (c3) is handled by keeping stepwise weaning for them. Reporting follows SQUIRE 2.0.
alternatives: Before-after cohort comparison of the 2025 to 2026 and 2026 to 2027 seasons (refused: season severity and staffing confound it, and the protocol could not be adapted)
Direct cessation for all ages (refused: unresolved safety evidence under 8 weeks, claim c3)
Leave weaning to individual attendings (the status quo that produces 52-hour medians)
whyNotMoreComplex: A multi-site trial would be needed to settle the young-infant question; this ward's question is local improvement, which run charts and balancing measures can answer in one season.

decision.statement: Introduce the direct-cessation weaning protocol for infants aged 8 weeks or older in PDSA cycles from November 2026 to March 2027, keeping stepwise weaning for younger infants, with a weekly run chart of time on high flow and re-escalation, PICU transfer and 7-day readmission as balancing measures.
decision.question: Should the ward adopt a direct-cessation weaning protocol for infants with bronchiolitis, and for which infants?

criteria.text: Direct cessation shortened time on high flow without a clear rise in re-escalation in a trial and a ward report.
Re-escalation within 24 hours among infants aged 8 weeks or older exceeds 15 percent over any four-week period.

gates.requirement: Quality committee screening of the protocol as quality improvement
gates.evidence: Screening QC-PED-2026-044 dated 2026-09-15, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Sign-off of the weaning protocol by the PICU and ward medical leads
gates.evidence: Protocol version 1.2 signed off 2026-09-18, supplied by the investigator

alternatives: Before-after cohort comparison of two seasons
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1, c2 and c4 for the change and on c3 (high uncertainty) for the age limit; both gates are met on investigator-supplied records.

summary: Quality improvement with PDSA cycles recommended; the design is resolved here, and the decision limits the protocol to infants aged 8 weeks or older.
